title: Relationship between circulating senescence-associated secretory phenotype levels and severity of type 2 diabetes-associated periodontitis: A cross-sectional study.
authors: Song, Xiuxiu; Yue, Ziqi; Fan, Linli; Zou, Haonan; Zhao, Pengfei; Nie, Lulingxiao; Zhu, Kangjian; Jiang, Jingjing; Lv, Qingguo; Wang, Qi
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨循环SASP水平与2型糖尿病相关牙周炎严重程度的关系，属于临床血清标志物关联分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) has recently been found to drive comorbid diabetes and periodontitis by inducing a chronic, low-degree inflammatory state. Here, we sought to explore the relationship between circulating SASP and the severity of type 2 diabetes-associated periodontitis (DP). METHODS: Eighty patients (middle-aged periodontitis, M-P group; aged periodontitis, A-P group; M-DP group; and A-DP group; n = 20) provided gingival epithelium, serum, and periodontal clinical parameters. Circulating levels of 12 DP-related SASP factors were analyzed by immunoassay. Correlation between periodontal clinical parameters and circulating SASP levels was analyzed by Spearman's rank correlation coefficient and back propagation artificial neural network (BPNN). Senescence markers (p16, p21, and HMGB1) in gingiva were determined by immunofluorescence assay. RESULTS: M-DP group had increased serum levels of twelve SASP factors compared with the M-P group (p < 0.5). Serum levels of IL-6, IL-4, and RAGE were higher in the A-DP group than the A-P group (p < 0.5). The circulating concentrations of certain SASP proteins, including IL-1beta, IL-4, MMP-8, OPG, RANKL, and RAGE were correlated with the clinical parameters of DP. BPNN showed that serum SASP levels had considerable predictive value for CAL of DP. Additionally, the DP group had higher expressions of p16, p21, and cytoplasmic-HMGB1 in the gingiva than the P group (p < 0.5). CONCLUSIONS: Significantly enhanced circulating SASP levels and aggravated periodontal destruction were observed in patients with DP. Importantly, a non-negligible association between serum SASP levels and the severity of DP was found.
abstract_zh: 背景：近期研究发现，衰老相关分泌表型（SASP）通过诱导慢性低度炎症状态，驱动糖尿病与牙周炎的共病发生。本研究旨在探讨循环SASP水平与2型糖尿病相关牙周炎（DP）严重程度之间的关系。方法：80名患者（中年牙周炎组，M-P组；老年牙周炎组，A-P组；中年DP组，M-DP组；老年DP组，A-DP组；每组n=20）提供牙龈上皮、血清及牙周临床参数。通过免疫分析检测12种DP相关SASP因子的循环水平。采用Spearman秩相关系数和反向传播人工神经网络（BPNN）分析牙周临床参数与循环SASP水平之间的相关性。通过免疫荧光法测定牙龈中的衰老标志物（p16、p21和HMGB1）。结果：与M-P组相比，M-DP组血清中十二种SASP因子水平升高（p < 0.5）。A-DP组血清IL-6、IL-4和RAGE水平高于A-P组（p < 0.5）。某些SASP蛋白（包括IL-1beta、IL-4、MMP-8、OPG、RANKL和RAGE）的循环浓度与DP的临床参数相关。BPNN显示，血清SASP水平对DP的CAL具有显著的预测价值。此外，DP组牙龈中p16、p21和胞质HMGB1的表达高于P组（p < 0.5）。结论：在DP患者中观察到循环SASP水平显著升高和牙周破坏加剧。重要的是，血清SASP水平与DP严重程度之间存在不可忽视的关联。
